text:
Devon: heads-up: reserved pool in us-west-2 is at 100% GPU util for ~4m. queue depth spiked to ~650, p95 wait ~12s, lots of 429s returning for low-tier tenants.
Maria: yeah saw the alert. admission controller flipped into backpressure, but retries are amplifying the tail.
ops-bot: [ALERT] reserved-pool-usw2 utilization=100% queue_depth=648 backpressure=ON
Ryan: looks like a single customer (atlas) is running a large eval with very long sequences — accounts for ~42% of active tokens right now.
Kari: short list of immediate mitigations: 1) cap per-tenant concurrency/weight, 2) route non-SLA traffic to hosted fallback model, 3) tighten admission reclaim thresholds.
Devon: I'm going to patch the admission controller thresholds now — observed reclaim floor was too low and blocked eviction on idle KV sessions. pushing small hotfix.
Devon: applying change: 
```
admit.reclaim_min_ratio = 0.20  # was 0.12
admit.max_queue_per_gpu = 120   # lower queue spike tolerance
```
Maria: ping @support to call affected customers with priority SLAs and flag for on-call sales.
Ryan: starting canary reroute for atlas -> hosted-fallback:model-micro (10% -> 50% -> 100%). will monitor latency and token e2e.
ops-bot: deploy triggered: ryan/canary/reroute-2034 status=STARTED
Amanda: after canary at 50% we see p95 drop from 12s -> 5.6s for reserved pool, queue depth down to ~240.
Kari: good. also create a temporary tenant-weight rule to pinch heavy eval jobs until we scale capacity. I'll open a policy change to enforce eval quotas.
Devon: found root cause: admission reclaim was skipping tenants with active KV sessions due to a logic bug; hotfix branch `hot/admit-reclaim-fix` created. will roll to prod after quick test.
Maria: Ops: coordinate with infra to request a short-term dedicated burst (preemptible GPUs) for the evening window. Cost team ok with emergency bump.
Ryan: rolling hotfix now to admission controller canary lane.
ops-bot: canary deploy complete: ryan/canary/reroute-2034 status=SUCCESS
Amanda: post-hotfix we see sustained queue reduction and 429s down 87%. customer-facing errors reduced.
Kari: next steps: schedule capacity add for 2hrs, add admission-controller unit test for KV edge-case, and owner to run a postmortem.
Devon: filing follow-up: github.com/redwood/infrastructure/issues/4567 - admit reclaim bug + remediation steps.
Maria: assigning postmortem and stakeholder notify (support, sales, finance). tags: capacity, admission-control, reserved-pool.
Devon: marking incident as mitigated; will continue to monitor for 30m then transition to monitoring. thanks all. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: [INFO] incident mitigated by Devon. Monitoring window started (30m).
